subject: Workplace Skills
title: Framing Your Proposal
description: A micro-lesson that makes Framing Your Proposal usable.

hook.text: 'Cut 20% of features' was rejected. 'Focus on the top 80% that drive revenue' was approved. Same action.

buildup.text: How you frame an idea determines how it's received. The same proposal succeeds or fails on language alone.

discovery.text: Frame proposals in terms of what the audience values. Revenue for the CFO. User impact for the CPO.

twist.text: Framing is not spin. It's selecting the most relevant angle for a specific audience. The facts stay the same.

climax.text: Before presenting, ask: 'What does this person measure success by?' Frame your ask in those terms.

punchline.text: Same idea. Different frame. Completely different outcome.

quiz.question: What is the key to effectively framing a proposal?
options: Using the most technical language possible
Presenting it in terms of what the audience values
Making the proposal as long and detailed as possible
